chunks: Sa'd narrated that from Musa ibn al-Husayn and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: I join these people in the maghrib salat (prayer), and they hasten me such that I do not have the chance to give the adhan and iqamah, and I recite nothing but al-Hamd until he bows. Will that suffice me? He said: Yes, al-Hamd alone suffices you.
And it is possible that the report is specific to the state of taqiyyah, for that is permissible when one performs the ruku' and sujud.

key_terms.أُؤَذِّنَ: to give the adhan, the call to prayer
key_terms.أُقِيمَ: to give the iqamah, the commencement call for salat
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary concealment in a situation of danger
key_terms.الْحَمْدَ: Surat al-Hamd, meaning Surat al-Fatihah recited in salat
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib salat (prayer), the sunset ritual prayer
key_terms.يُجْزِيكَ: it suffices you or fulfills the requirement for you

ai.seo_question: Is reciting only al-Hamd sufficient in maghrib salat when praying in taqiyyah behind those not followed?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for one who prays maghrib behind those whom one does not follow, in a circumstance of haste. The Imam عليه السلام states that reciting only al-Hamd is sufficient, and the appended note indicates that this may be specific to a situation of taqiyyah, provided that ruku' and sujud are performed.
